2. Facts, relevant for disposal of this Rule, in brief, are that, Kazi Monzur Ahmed and 8 others (who are the opposite parties in this matter), as plaintiffs, had filed Civil Suit No.237 of 2003, before the Assistant Judge, Keranigonj, Dhaka, against the Government Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, seeking declaration of title in respect of the suit property described in the schedule to the plaint. The case of the plaintiffs is that they are the owner of the suit property comprising 34¾ decimals of land at CS/SA plot No. 272 under CS Khatian No.733 and SA Khatian No.643, Mouja-Chankutia, PS Keranigonj, District-Dhaka. They have narrated the facts in their plaint as to how they have acquired title in the suit property and that the suit plot had been recorded in the name of the plaintiffs during RS survey operation, being RS Khas Khatian No.l. Accordingly, they have prayed for declaration of title in respect of the suit property as well as that the disputed RS Khatian was not lawful etc. 

 3. The defendant has contested in the suit by filing written statement in which the Government has denied all material allegations made in the plaint and further stated, in paragraph No.15 of the written statement that, the suit property being'RS Khatian No.701 has been recorded in Khas Khatian No.1 (RS Khatian No.1), since, it was an alluviated land and the title of the suit property vested in the Government in accordance with law. They have denied contention made in the plaint. 

 10. The learned Advocate Mr Azharullah Bhuiyan with Mr Md Parvez Chowdhury, have appeared for the opposite party No.1-9. Mr Bhuiyan submits that, the trial court has rightly discussed the evidence on record and decreed the suit and the appellate court has also rightly affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. He submits that, the case of the Government is that, it has acquired title in the suit property which is an alluvial land and therefore, recorded in the name of the Government as Khas Khatian (in RS Khatian No.1). But the government could not produce any documentary evidence to show that, suit property was alluvial land, nor they have submitted any oral and documentary evidence to prove their case. He submits that, both the courts below have found title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property and that there is no infirmity in the impugned judgment and decree that may call for interference by this court. He also submits that, there is no misreading and non reading of the evidence. He concludes submits that, the courts below have committed no error of law in passing the impugned judgment and decree, nor the same has resulted in any error in the decision and occasioned failure of justice. Therefore, he submits that, this Rule has no merit and the same is liable to be discharged.
